Domain Expectations: MediaItem validates nonblank id/title and positive durationMillis; exposes getters for id, title, durationMillis

Playlist stores MediaItem instances (ArrayList), rejects null adds, and provides size/getAt/removeAt with standard semantics; hasNext/hasPrevious and nextIndex/previousIndex are bounds-safe, returning -1 for empty lists
PlayerState zero-arg constructor sets currentIndex=0, positionMillis=0, status=STOPPED; setters validate non-negative position and non-null status; resetPosition sets position to 0

VolumeControl starts with volume=100, lastNonMuted=100, muted=false; setVolume assigns both volume and lastNonMuted even when muted; mute flips muted=true without changing volumes; unmute restores volume=lastNonMuted; getEffectiveVolume returns 0 when muted else volume
DeterministicClock starts at 0, rejects negative advances, and adds nonnegative deltas only
PlaybackController.play rejects an empty playlist; for nonempty playlists, accept index 0, reset position to zero only if already at duration, and set status=PLAYING
onClockAdvanced uses nonnegative delta since lastTick, advances only when status=PLAYING, clamps at duration, and switches status to STOPPED while keeping position exactly at duration

PlayerSnapshot.from returns an immutable snapshot: for invalid/empty index use empty title and duration 0; for valid index return the real media metadata with current position, status, and volume/mute state
Domain Reasoning: Playback progression must be driven by a deterministic in-memory clock (DeterministicClock) only; time is advanced explicitly via advance(deltaMillis) and observed via onClockAdvanced()
PlaybackController governs PlayerState transitions among STOPPED, PLAYING, and PAUSED, clamping position within [0, duration] and switching to STOPPED exactly at end-of-media
Playlist provides safe navigation (next/previous with clamped indices) and supports empty-playlist edge cases
PlayerState zero-arg constructor MUST initialize currentIndex=0, positionMillis=0, status=STOPPED; initializing currentIndex to -1 is forbidden
VolumeControl tracks volume [0,100], mute flag, and lastNonMuted with the rule: setVolume always updates both volume and lastNonMuted even while muted; unmute restores lastNonMuted
PlayerSnapshot aggregates a read-only projection combining playlist metadata, player state, and volume, providing safe defaults for empty/invalid index
Seek operations clamp to the current item's duration; next/previous change index using Playlist helpers and reset position only when index actually changes

- PlayerState is a public final class owning nested enum PlaybackStatus { STOPPED, PLAYING, PAUSED }. - VolumeControl is a public final class initialized with volume=100, lastNonMuted=100, muted=false. setVolume validates [0,100], always assigns both `this.volume = volume` and `this.lastNonMuted = volume`, including while muted. mute sets muted=true without changing those fields; unmute sets muted=false and assigns volume=lastNonMuted; getEffectiveVolume returns muted?0:volume. A setVolume call while muted therefore changes the value restored by unmute; preserving the pre-mute value instead is forbidden
- DeterministicClock is a public final class with currentTimeMillis=0, getCurrentTimeMillis(), and advance(long deltaMillis) rejecting negative delta and adding nonnegative delta. No wall clock, Thread.sleep, timer, randomness, GUI, filesystem, or network is used

- PlaybackController is a public final class constructed from nonnull Playlist, VolumeControl, DeterministicClock; it creates a PlayerState (therefore index 0) and stores lastTick=clock.getCurrentTimeMillis(). play rejects an empty playlist, accepts index 0 for a nonempty playlist, resets position to zero only if already at duration, and sets PLAYING. pause sets PAUSED. stop sets STOPPED and position zero. seek clamps to [0,current duration]. next/previous use Playlist bounds helpers, reset position only when index actually changes, and remain at last/first index at bounds. onClockAdvanced computes nonnegative delta from lastTick, advances only while PLAYING, clamps at duration and changes to STOPPED while keeping position exactly duration. getSnapshot/getState/getPlaylist/getVolumeControl expose the canonical objects
- Main.java constructs a small in-memory playlist and deterministic clock, runs a bounded demo, and exits without input or loops. pom.xml compiles source/target 11 and uses only JUnit Jupiter test dependency with Surefire
- MainTest.java contains exactly three JUnit Jupiter @Test methods. Test 2: two items durations 3000/4000; initial play succeeds at index0; seek(5000) clamps to3000; next makes index1/position0, a second next remains index1; previous makes index0, a second previous remains index0. UI / UX / Interaction Design draft: Headless core only; no GUI. Main.java constructs an in-memory playlist and a deterministic clock, runs a small, bounded demonstration sequence (play, advance, snapshot), prints minimal information or none, and exits without loops or input. All user-facing behaviors are represented through method calls and snapshot data for tests.
User Stories: As a user, I can play, pause, and stop a media item from a playlist and see accurate position tracking.
As a user, I can seek within the current media item with clamping at the media duration.
As a user, I can navigate to next or previous items, staying at bounds when already at the last or first item.
As a user, I can adjust volume, mute/unmute, and expect unmute to restore the most recently set volume even if set while muted.
As a user, I can retrieve a snapshot of the current playback state and metadata at any time.
